package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"sort"
)

// The concrete (non-generic) in-place sorters reorder the interpreter's own
// backing array through the transport writeback. An aliasing slice header must
// observe the same reordering, and capacity beyond the sorted length must be
// left untouched — exactly as native Go behaves.
func main() {
	s := []int{5, 3, 4, 1, 2}
	alias := s
	sort.Ints(s)
	fmt.Println("sorted:", s)
	fmt.Println("alias:", alias)

	words := []string{"pear", "apple", "fig", "cherry"}
	sort.Strings(words)
	fmt.Println("words:", words)

	// Only the visible length is reordered; the trailing capacity is preserved.
	backing := []int{7, 6, 5, 4}
	head := backing[:2]
	sort.Ints(head)
	fmt.Println("head:", head)
	fmt.Println("backing:", backing)

	prices := []float64{2.5, 1.25, 3.75}
	sort.Float64s(prices)
	fmt.Println("prices:", prices)
}
